rows.rationale: Vendor affirms a documented Information Security Program; no inherent risk answer makes this insufficient.
Vendor claims an ISO/IEC 27001 certified ISMS, but no certificate has been seen.
rows.evidenceToRequest: Current ISO/IEC 27001 certificate with scope statement and certifying body name and expiry date.

rows.rationale: Certificate is offered only on request, so PUC has not yet seen it.
rows.evidenceToRequest: Current ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, provided before rating is finalized.

rows.rationale: Vendor affirms executive leadership reviews information security.
Vendor affirms MFA for employee access to corporate systems, relevant given IRA-04 system access.
Vendor affirms regular review of privileged accounts; IRA-05 says the vendor needs no privileged access to PUC systems.
Vendor affirms prompt access removal on termination, relevant given IRA-04 system access.
Vendor affirms encryption in transit for confidential client information, which IRA-01 says will be shared.
Vendor affirms encryption at rest for confidential client information, which IRA-01 says will be shared.
Vendor affirms documented retention and disposal procedures for data it holds.
Vendor does not commit to storing PUC data in Canada, and residency is undetermined, while regulatory requirements apply.

conflict.note: IRA-13 (data leaving the country) is Unknown and IRA-14 says regulatory requirements apply, yet the vendor has not committed to Canadian residency.

rows.evidenceToRequest: Written data residency commitment for PUC data, stating storage and processing locations, and any offshore access.

rows.rationale: Vendor affirms a documented Incident Response Plan.
Vendor affirms periodic incident response exercises.
Vendor says it will notify PUC of incidents affecting engagement data, but gives no timeline and it is not shown as contractual.
rows.evidenceToRequest: Contractual incident notification clause with a stated notification timeline.

rows.rationale: Vendor affirms BC and DR plans, relevant because IRA-07 marks the service as business-critical.
Vendor says recovery plans are tested periodically, but no test results are provided for a business-critical service.

conflict.note: IRA-07 marks the service as business-critical, so untested recovery plans would matter more.

rows.evidenceToRequest: Summary of the most recent recovery plan test, with date and outcome.

rows.rationale: Vendor claims a completed SOC 2 Type II audit, but the report has not been seen.
rows.evidenceToRequest: Current SOC 2 Type II report with audit period and any exceptions noted.

rows.rationale: Executive summary is offered only under NDA, so PUC has not seen it.
rows.evidenceToRequest: Executive summary of the SOC 2 Type II report, received under NDA.

rows.rationale: Vendor affirms periodic independent penetration tests.
Vendor affirms it maintains a third-party risk management program.
Vendor affirms risk-based due diligence and lifecycle reassessment of critical third parties and subcontractors.
Vendor says subcontractors are subject to security requirements, but IRA-12 says subcontractor involvement is still Unknown.

conflict.note: IRA-12 is Unknown, so the subcontractor security requirements cannot be checked against actual subcontractors.

rows.evidenceToRequest: Named list of any subcontractors and copies of the security clauses that flow down to them.

rows.rationale: Vendor says no subcontractors are expected, which is not a firm commitment, and IRA-12 is still Unknown.

conflict.note: IRA-12 is Unknown and the response only says subcontractors are not expected, so involvement is not ruled out.

rows.evidenceToRequest: Written confirmation that no subcontractors will be used, or a full list of any that will be, with the flow-down clauses.

rows.rationale: Vendor affirms internal policies on responsible AI use, relevant to an AI governance engagement.
Vendor affirms employees receive guidance on appropriate AI use.
Vendor states customer information will not be used to train AI models.

iraInconsistencies.note: The service is marked business-critical but an outage is marked as not significantly impacting operations, which needs reconciling.
Regulatory requirements are marked as applicable but no regulated information is marked as processed, so the basis for the regulatory applicability should be confirmed.
The vendor is marked as accessing internal systems but not as needing privileged access or connecting to the corporate network, so the access method should be confirmed.
